contracts.commit_point: The two Runner.run invocation sites gate the commit: main.py:98-100 (MainLegalAgent on user_input) and main.py:107-109 (LegalAnalysisAgent on decision.document_content); the tripwire decision is produced within the guardrail at guardrails.py:47-57 and enforced where InputGuardrailTripwireTriggered is caught at main.py:126-128, which discards the run result and blocks the input.
contracts.declared_mechanism: sensitive_input_guardrail, declared with the @input_guardrail decorator (guardrails.py:28-33), which extracts the last user-role message (guardrails.py:36-40), runs sensitive_check_agent via Runner.run (guardrails.py:47; checker agent configured at guardrails.py:20-25 with guardrail_instructions from agent_instructions.py:37-38), and returns GuardrailFunctionOutput with tripwire_triggered=result.final_output.contains_sensitive_info (guardrails.py:54-57); registered on analysis_agent via input_guardrails=[sensitive_input_guardrail] (main.py:45) and on main_agent (main.py:70); a raised InputGuardrailTripwireTriggered is caught at main.py:126-128, logging the trigger and printing 'Input blocked' so the run result is abandoned.
contracts.forbidden_condition: The content evaluated at the guarded run is judged by the sensitive_check_agent to contain sensitive personal information (email, phone, SSN, CNIC, etc.), i.e. result.final_output.contains_sensitive_info is true, causing the guardrail to return tripwire_triggered=true.

contracts.protected_operation: Runner.run execution of MainLegalAgent on console user_input (main.py:98-100) and Runner.run execution of LegalAnalysisAgent on decision.document_content taken from the MainLegalAgent run output (main.py:107-109), each of which forwards the input through the configured model (model/client imported from model.py at main.py:25; RunConfig at main.py:85).
contracts.protected_resource: The model-facing processing pipeline of MainLegalAgent and LegalAnalysisAgent and their configured LLM model/provider — the destination to which the guarded input would be transmitted by the run.
contracts.protection_obligation: Agent runs must not proceed when the incoming content contains sensitive personal information (email, phone, SSN, CNIC, etc.): the registered sensitive_input_guardrail must trip the run so that MainLegalAgent is not executed on raw user input and LegalAnalysisAgent is not executed on the agent-extracted document content, blocking that content from being committed to the model-facing agent run. (Merges both reviewers' duplicate wording for the same obligation.)
scope_limits: Detection is an LLM judgment by sensitive_check_agent (guardrails.py:20-25, 47) using guardrail_instructions (agent_instructions.py:37-38); the contract only covers inputs the checker flags as containing sensitive info.
The guardrail inspects only the last user-role message of the input (guardrails.py:36-40); earlier conversation turns are not scanned.

The guardrail is registered only on main_agent (main.py:70) and analysis_agent (main.py:45); the casual_chat branch (main.py:118-120), the friendly_agent run (main.py:110-114), and the sub-agents exposed as tools (main.py:49-62, 71-76) are not shown to carry this input guardrail.

Whether the SDK runs input guardrails concurrently with the first model response, and whether a tripwire aborts an in-flight model request or only discards its result, is a runtime question not decidable from the supplied source.
